what: Bairagis (Vishnu) and Gosains (Siva) described as two castes of ascetics who have fallen from self-sacrifice and hold proprietary rights in many villages
quote: The Bairagis and Gosains are two castes of ascetics, the devotees respectively of Vishnu and Siva.

what: Several Gosain families hold considerable estates in Raipur
quote: In Raipur several Gosain families hold considerable estates.

what: Theory of origin of estates: Mahants of popular temples invested temple surplus in land/moneylending and became proprietors; the Feudatory States of Nandgaon and Chhuikhadan belong to Bairagi families obtained this way
quote: Besides the estates in Raipur and Bilaspur, the Feudatory States of Nandgaon and Chhuikiiadan belong to Hairfigi families and were obtained in the same manner.

what: Tahutdar family of Lormi (about 100 villages) are Bairagis; taluk given in charity to Baramdas Bairagi in 1826 by the Raja of Nagpur; chela Lakhmidas succeeded 1853; estate now divided among four brothers
quote: It is said that the taluk was originally given in charity to one Baramdas Bairagi in 1826 by the Raja of Nagpur.

what: Rule of caste: celibate Bairagi selects a chela to inherit; in important families celibacy abandoned, men marry; monasteries 'dens of wickedness' (quoted)
quote: But in the important families the practice of celibacy has been abandoned and the men marry and have families in the ordinary manner.

what: Math of the Nihang (celibate) Bairagi gaddi: Mahant Gautamdas, 12th successor; 6 revenue-free + 12 ordinary villages (Samvat 1915 acquisitions); founder Dayaramdas from Gwalior; list of six Swamis; Darbari, arms-act exempt
quote: Mahant Gautamdas claims to be the 1 2th successor of X\it Nihang gaddi of Seorinarayan. (Among Nihang Bairagis marriage is forbidden ) He has his math at Seorinarayan*

what: Village has two mahals: Mahantpara (proprietor Gautam Das Mahant) and Bhogahapara (Jadunath Bhogaha, who feeds the deities and religious mendicants, holds six revenue-free villages)
quote: The village consists of two separate mahals^ known as Mahantpara and Bhogahapara.

what: Gautam Das Mahant, Bairagi of Seorinarayan, among prominent moneylenders
quote: Other prominent men are Gautam Das Mahant, Bairagi of Seorinarayan

what: Bairagis hold 156 villages of 2242 as proprietors (fourth landholding caste after Brahmans, Banias, Kurmis); Gosains not separately listed
quote: the Bairagis with 156, the Chamars with 148, the Rajputs with 226

what: Proprietor of Takhatpur is a Bairagi lady
quote: The prot 'prietor is a Bairagi lady.

what: Gosains followers of the sterner Sivite creed have taken up arms; Naga Gosains a fighting band, went nearly naked; quelled a rebellion of the Raja of Bastar for the Marathas and leaders were given land grants in Raipur
quote: The Naga Gosains were a well-known band of fighters who went about nearly naked, having nothing but a skin round their loins.

what: A Gosain was Bhaskar Pant's representative in Ratanpur (Maratha period) and was ousted by Raghunathsingh
quote: Raghunathsingh ousted his representative, a Gosain, and once more assumed the reins of government.

what: Kabirpanthi Mahants: headquarters at Kawardha, fair at Kudarmal (Magh), disputed succession of Dhirajnam and Ugranam; Dharam Das ancestry
quote: The Mahants of Kawardha claim to be the direct descendants of Dharam Das.

what: Kabirpanthi fair in Magh for 7-8 days; converts initiated; grave of Churaman, first Mahant
quote: A Kabirpanthi fair is held here in the month of Magh lasting for seven or eight days, at which converts are initiated as members of the sect.

what: Satnami Chamars hold a fair at Ratanpur on the same date
quote: The Satnami Chamars have a fair at Ratanpur on the same date
